meta.source: Sheldon Ross, A First Course in Probability, 10th ed. — encounters are ORIGINAL problems mirroring the book's problem archetypes; 'mirrors' gives book problem refs (P = Problem, ST = Self-Test, Ex = Example, TE = Theoretical Exercise).

encounters.title: The Gate Seal
encounters.story: Tallyburg's gate seal is {L} letters (A-Z) followed by {D} digit-runes (0-9). The guard laughs: 'Nobody can try them all.' Prove him right.

phases.ask: How many seals exist if symbols may repeat?
The new rule bans any repeated letter or repeated digit. How many seals now?

hints: Is the seal built in stages, where each stage's options don't depend on which symbol you picked earlier?
Once a letter is used and repeats are banned, how many letters are left for the next slot?
solution: Each slot is a stage, so multiply the options per slot (basic counting principle).
With repetition: 26 per letter slot and 10 per digit slot → 26^L·10^D.
Without repetition the count drops by one each slot: 26·25·… and 10·9·… = P(26,L)·P(10,D).

encounters.title: Wheel of the Night Market
encounters.story: A merchant's wheel has {S} equal sectors. You spin it {R} times and he records the sequence of sectors.

phases.ask: How many different recorded sequences are possible?

hints: Does an earlier spin change how many sectors the next spin can land on?
solution: Each spin has S outcomes regardless of earlier spins → S·S·…·S = S^R.

encounters.title: Night Watch Posts
encounters.story: {N} guards must cover {N} different watch posts, one guard per post.

phases.ask: Two of the guards are archers and may only take the 2 tower posts (in either order); the others go anywhere left. How many assignments now?

hints: Fill post 1, then post 2… how many guards are left each time?
Handle the restricted guards first. In how many ways can they fill the towers? Then how many ways are there for everyone else?
solution: N guards to N posts is an ordering of the guards: N!.
Archers fill the 2 towers in 2! ways; the remaining N−2 guards fill the remaining posts in (N−2)! ways; multiply.
encounters.pattern: assign n things to n slots → n!; restricted items first

encounters.title: Courier Codes
encounters.story: A courier code is: a colour (one of 7), then a vowel (A, E, I, O, U), then a digit that must NOT be 0.
hints: Count the allowed options at each position separately. Which position has a restriction?
encounters.pattern: restricted slots → count each slot's allowed set

encounters.title: The Banner Weaver
encounters.story: The weaver stitches the letters of BANANAS onto a banner in any order. Identical letters look identical.

phases.ask: How many distinct banners can she make?

hints: If every letter were a different colour, how many orders would there be?
How many times is each banner counted if you secretly swap the identical A's among themselves? And the N's?
solution: Each distinct banner is counted 3! (A's) × 2! (N's) times.

encounters.title: The Feast Bench
encounters.story: {N} heroes sit on one long bench. Two of them, Asha and Bodhi, are inseparable.

phases.ask: In how many orders can they sit if Asha and Bodhi must sit together?
In how many orders do Asha and Bodhi NOT sit together?

hints: Glue Asha and Bodhi into one block. How many units are you arranging now?
Inside the block, how many internal orders are there?
Is 'not together' easier to count directly or as total minus together?
solution: Block trick: (N−1) units → (N−1)! orders, times 2 internal orders.
encounters.pattern: 'must be together' → glue into a block; 'not together' → complement

encounters.title: The Guild Library
encounters.story: The librarian shelves {a} novels, {b} maths books and {c} chemistry books (all different). Books of the same subject must stay together.

phases.ask: How many shelf arrangements are possible?

hints: First decide the order of the subject blocks. How many ways?
Then, inside each block, how many ways can its books be ordered?
encounters.pattern: blocks: order the blocks × order inside each block

encounters.title: Repeating Vault Digits
encounters.story: Vault combinations are 3 digits from 000 to 999. The thief only tries combinations with repeated digits.

phases.ask: How many combinations have at least two equal digits?
How many have exactly two equal digits?

hints: 'At least two equal': what is the opposite event, and is it easier to count?
Which combinations have 'at least two' but not 'exactly two'?
solution: All different: 10·9·8 = 720, so at least two equal = 1000 − 720 = 280.
Remove the 10 with all three equal: 270.

encounters.title: Festival Honours
encounters.story: {k} different festival honours are awarded among {n} apprentices.

phases.ask: How many outcomes if one apprentice may win several honours?
How many outcomes if nobody may win more than one?

hints: Think honour by honour: how many possible winners does each honour have?
solution: With repeats allowed each honour has n choices: n^k.
encounters.pattern: distinct items to people: with reuse → n^k, without → P(n,k)

encounters.title: The Toast
encounters.story: At the guild feast all {n} members clink cups with every other member exactly once.
hints: A clink is a pair of people. Does the order within the pair matter?
solution: Each clink is an unordered pair: C(n,2).

encounters.title: Lantern Dance
encounters.story: From {w} women and {m} men, {k} of each are chosen and then paired off into {k} mixed dance pairs.

phases.ask: How many different results are possible?

hints: Split it into stages: choose the women, choose the men, then pair them. How many ways is each stage?
solution: Pair: woman 1 has k partners, woman 2 has k−1, … → k!.

encounters.title: The Mixed Council
encounters.story: A council needs 2 smiths (from {A}), 2 weavers (from {B}) and 3 millers (from {Cc}).
hints: Is choosing the smiths independent of choosing the weavers?

encounters.title: The Feuding Pair
encounters.story: You invite {k} of your {n} friends to a feast, but two of them refuse to attend together.

phases.ask: How many guest lists are possible?

hints: Count all lists, then ask: how many lists contain BOTH feuding friends?
solution: Lists with both feuders: fix them, choose k−2 from the other n−2.
encounters.pattern: forbidden pair → total minus lists containing both

encounters.title: The Balanced Committee
encounters.story: A 6-member committee is drawn from {men} men and {women} women. It must contain at least 3 women and at least 2 men.
hints: List the possible (women, men) splits that obey both rules.
Count each split separately. Do the splits overlap?
encounters.pattern: 'at least' constraints → enumerate disjoint cases and add

encounters.title: The Street Grid
encounters.story: From the inn (bottom-left) to the castle you walk only right or up: {R} blocks right and {U} up.

phases.ask: How many shortest routes are there?
How many of them pass the well at ({a} right, {b} up)?

hints: A route is a word made of R's and U's. How many letters, and how many are U?
Split the trip at the well: routes to the well × routes from the well.
solution: Choose which of the R+U steps are 'up': C(R+U,U).
Through a point: multiply the two legs.
encounters.pattern: grid paths → choose positions of one step type

encounters.title: Rune of Expansion
encounters.story: The rune-smith expands (2x − y)^{n}.

phases.ask: What is the coefficient of x^{i}·y^(n−i)?

hints: In the binomial theorem, which term gives x^i? Remember the 2 and the minus sign come along with x and y.

encounters.title: Squad Assignment
encounters.story: {a}+{b}+{c} recruits are split into the Scouts ({a}), the Guards ({b}) and the Builders ({c}).
hints: Choose the Scouts first, then the Guards from those left. What is left for the Builders?
encounters.pattern: labelled groups of given sizes → multinomial

encounters.title: Pick-up Teams
encounters.story: {g}×{s} kids split themselves into {g} teams of {s}. The teams have no names or colours.
hints: First pretend the teams are labelled. How many divisions?
How many times is each unlabelled division counted when labels are added?
solution: Each unlabelled division is counted g! times (permute the labels) → divide by g!.
encounters.pattern: unlabelled equal groups → divide by (number of groups)!

encounters.title: Watchtower Scouts
encounters.story: {n} scouts are sent to {t} watchtowers.

phases.ask: How many assignments if any tower may get any number of scouts?
How many if each tower must get exactly {n}/{t} scouts?

hints: Think scout by scout: how many tower choices does each scout have?
Fixed sizes per tower: which formula counts labelled groups of fixed sizes?
solution: Each scout picks a tower: t^n.
encounters.pattern: free assignment → t^n; fixed sizes → multinomial

encounters.title: Nationalities on the Podium
encounters.story: A tournament has {a} players from the North, {b} from the South, {c} from the East and {d} from the West. The scroll only records each finisher's region, in finishing order.

phases.ask: How many different scrolls are possible?

hints: The scroll is a word of region letters. Which letters repeat, and how many times?
solution: Arrangements of a word with repeats: n!/(a!b!c!d!).
encounters.pattern: only types recorded → arrangement with repeats

encounters.title: Coins in Chests
encounters.story: You have {n} identical gold coins and {r} treasure chests.

phases.ask: How many ways if every chest must get at least one coin?
How many ways if chests may be empty?
How many ways if you may also keep some coins (not all distributed)?

hints: Line the coins up. Placing dividers in the gaps splits them into chests. How many gaps are there?
Trick: add 1 coin per chest first, then distribute. What is the new total?
Keeping coins = a hidden extra chest.
solution: Positive solutions: choose r−1 of the n−1 gaps: C(n−1,r−1).
encounters.pattern: identical items into distinct boxes → stars and bars

encounters.title: Triple Rune
encounters.story: The smith expands (x₁ + x₂ + x₃)^6.

phases.ask: What is the coefficient of x₁²·x₂·x₃³?

hints: Which theorem generalises the binomial theorem to more than two terms?

encounters.title: No Couples on Patrol
encounters.story: From {c} married couples, a patrol of {k} people is chosen. No married couple may serve together.
hints: First choose which couples are represented. Then, from each chosen couple, how many choices?
encounters.pattern: 'at most one per pair' → choose pairs, then one from each

encounters.title: The Grand Deal
encounters.story: A full 52-card deck is dealt into 4 named hands of 13.

phases.ask: How many different deals are there? (Answer as an expression; the forge evaluates it.)

hints: The hands have names (North, East…). Which formula counts labelled groups of fixed sizes?

encounters.title: The Two-Draw Well
encounters.story: A well holds {k} differently coloured stones. You draw one, then draw again.

phases.ask: How many outcomes are in the sample space if you put the first stone back?
How many if you keep the first stone out?

hints: Write a few outcomes as ordered pairs. Can a pair repeat a colour in each case?
encounters.pattern: sample space = list of ordered outcomes

encounters.title: Two Exclusive Omens
encounters.story: Omens A and B can never both appear. P(A) = {a}, P(B) = {b}.

phases.ask: P(A appears but B does not)?

hints: Mutually exclusive means the circles don't overlap. What is P(AB)?
solution: AB^c = A because AB is empty.

encounters.title: Potions and Scrolls
encounters.story: In the market {a} of travellers carry a potion, {b} carry a scroll, and {ab} carry both.

phases.ask: P(a traveller carries at least one)?

hints: Draw two overlapping circles and fill in the overlap first. Then fill in each 'only' region.
solution: Exactly one = union − both = a + b − 2ab.
encounters.pattern: two-set inclusion–exclusion; fill the Venn from the inside out

encounters.title: Three Guilds
encounters.story: Of 100 villagers: {A} are in the Archers' guild, {B} in the Bakers', {Cc} in the Carpenters'. {AB} are Archers and Bakers, {AC} Archers and Carpenters, {BC} Bakers and Carpenters, and {ABC} are in all three.

phases.ask: How many villagers are in at least one guild?
How many are in exactly one guild?
A villager is picked at random. P(in no guild)?

hints: Start at the centre of the 3-circle Venn: put {ABC} there, then work outward.
'Exactly one' regions: take each circle and subtract its overlaps, but add the centre back.
solution: Union = sum of singles − sum of pairs + triple = 79.

encounters.title: The Gambler's Table
encounters.story: The rogue deals you 5 cards from a fair 52-card deck.

phases.ask: P(three of a kind, and nothing better)?

hints: Choose the ranks first, then the suits for each rank, then the leftover card(s).
Make sure the leftover cards can't accidentally make a better hand.
solution: Two pair: C(13,2) ranks for the pairs × C(4,2)² suits × 44 for the fifth card.
Three of a kind: 13·C(4,3) × C(12,2) other ranks × 4² suits.
encounters.pattern: equally likely hands: count favourable / C(52,5), ranks then suits

encounters.title: Bone Dice
encounters.story: Four fair dice are thrown together.

phases.ask: P(exactly one pair, with the other two different from it and from each other)?

hints: Use ordered outcomes (6^4 total). For one pair: which positions hold the pair? What value is the pair? What are the other two?
encounters.pattern: ordered outcomes keep everything equally likely

encounters.title: Royal Pair
encounters.story: Two cards are drawn. You win the 'royal pair' if one is a King and the other a Queen.
hints: Unordered: how many ways can you pick one King AND one Queen?

encounters.title: Twin Dice Oracle
encounters.story: Two fair dice are rolled.

phases.ask: P(the second die shows more than the first)?

hints: Lay out the 6×6 grid of outcomes. Which cells give the sum you want?
By symmetry, how do 'second > first' and 'first > second' compare? What is left over?
solution: Ties: 6 cells; the remaining 30 split evenly: 15/36.

encounters.title: Race of the Sums
encounters.story: Two dice are rolled again and again until the sum is 6 or 7. You win if 6 comes first.
hints: Rolls that are neither 6 nor 7 don't matter. Among the rolls that DO matter, what share are 6s?
solution: P(6) = 5/36, P(7) = 6/36. Given the game ends on a roll, P(6) = 5/11.

encounters.title: Craps in the Cellar
encounters.story: Craps: 7 or 11 on the first roll wins; 2, 3 or 12 loses. Otherwise your sum becomes the 'point', and you keep rolling until the point (win) or a 7 (lose).
hints: Split by the first roll. For a point p, use the race idea: P(p before 7).
Points 4 and 10 behave the same, as do 5 & 9 and 6 & 8.
solution: Point p: P(first roll = p)·P(p before 7) = n_p/36 · n_p/(n_p+6).
encounters.pattern: condition on the first step + race

encounters.title: Who Draws the Ruby?
encounters.story: A pouch has {r} rubies and {b} pebbles. Asha and Bodhi take turns drawing without replacement (Asha first). The first to draw a ruby wins.
hints: Asha wins if the first ruby appears on draw 1, 3, 5, …
P(first j draws are pebbles, then a ruby) = [C(b,j)/C(r+b,j)]·r/(r+b−j).
solution: Sum over the odd draw positions 1, 3, 5, … (j even pebbles before the first ruby).
encounters.pattern: sum over the turn on which the game ends

encounters.title: Three Stones
encounters.story: A sack holds {R} red, {B} blue and {G} green stones. You grab 3.
hints: 'Same colour' splits into three disjoint cases.
All different: one of each colour. How many ways?

encounters.title: Tagged Deer
encounters.story: A forest has {N} deer, and {T} of them wear a ranger's tag. Later, {n} deer are captured at random.
hints: Split the capture: choose the tagged ones from the tagged deer, and the untagged ones from the rest.

encounters.title: The Examiner's Scroll
encounters.story: The master gives {P} practice riddles; the exam uses {S} chosen at random. You can solve {K} of them.

phases.ask: P(you can solve every exam riddle)?
P(you can solve at least {S}−1 of them)?

hints: The exam is a random subset of size S. How many subsets lie entirely inside the ones you know?
solution: At least S−1: add the subsets with exactly one unknown riddle.

encounters.title: The Sock Drawer Puzzle
encounters.story: A drawer holds n socks, 5 of them red. Two socks are drawn and P(both red) = 2/9.
hints: Write P(both red) = C(5,2)/C(n,2) and solve for n.
encounters.pattern: set up the probability as an equation and solve

encounters.title: Inns of the Crossroads
encounters.story: {t} travellers each pick one of {h} inns at random, independently.

phases.ask: P(they all end up in different inns)?

hints: Count ordered outcomes. How many give all-different inns?

encounters.title: The Gambler of Méré
encounters.story: A gambler rolls one die {n} times and bets on getting at least one six.

phases.ask: Two dice are rolled repeatedly. What is the smallest number of rolls that makes P(at least one double six) ≥ 1/2?

hints: 'At least one' → what is P(none)?
Solve 1 − (35/36)^m ≥ 1/2 for m.

encounters.title: The Gap in the Line
encounters.story: {N} adventurers line up in random order, including Asha and Bodhi.

phases.ask: P(exactly one person stands between Asha and Bodhi)?

hints: Only the pair of positions taken by Asha and Bodhi matters. How many position pairs have a gap of exactly 2?
solution: Ordered position pairs at distance 2: 2(N−2) out of N(N−1).

encounters.title: The Ring of Keys
encounters.story: A ring has {n} keys and only one opens the cellar.

phases.ask: You try keys at random, putting failed ones aside. P(the door opens on try {k})?
Careless version: failed keys go back on the ring. P(it opens on try {k})?

hints: Without replacement: by symmetry, the correct key is equally likely to be in any position.
With replacement: the tries are independent.

encounters.title: Moons of Birth
encounters.story: How many people must be gathered so that P(at least two share a birth month) ≥ 1/2? (Assume all 12 months are equally likely.)
hints: Compute P(all different months) for n = 3, 4, 5…

encounters.title: The Second Smallest
encounters.story: 4 tokens are drawn from tokens numbered 1–12.

phases.ask: P(7 is the second smallest number drawn)?

hints: For 7 to be 2nd smallest: how many of the drawn tokens are below 7, and how many above?
encounters.pattern: fix the special value; split the rest

encounters.title: Two Patrols
encounters.story: {m} men and {m} women are randomly split into two patrols of {m}.

phases.ask: P(both patrols have the same number of men)?

hints: The first patrol determines the second. When do they have equal numbers of men?
solution: The first patrol needs m/2 men and m/2 women: C(m,m/2)²/C(2m,m).
encounters.pattern: choose one group; the complement is fixed

encounters.title: Mismatched Boots
encounters.story: A chest holds {p} pairs of boots. You grab {k} boots in the dark.
hints: Choose which pairs you take one boot from, then which boot from each.

encounters.title: The Cloakroom Curse
encounters.story: {n} knights hand in their helmets; the cursed cloakroom returns them at random.

phases.ask: P(at least one knight gets his own helmet)?

hints: Let A_i = knight i gets his own helmet. What is P(A_i), and what is P(A_i A_j)?
Inclusion–exclusion: the k-th term is C(n,k)·(n−k)!/n! = 1/k!.

encounters.title: The Missing Suit
encounters.story: You are dealt 13 cards.

phases.ask: P(your hand is missing at least one suit)?

hints: Let V_s = no cards of suit s. Why is the answer not simply 4·C(39,13)/C(52,13)?
Inclusion–exclusion over 1, 2 or 3 missing suits.

encounters.title: Four Banners
encounters.story: You are dealt 5 cards.

phases.ask: P(at least one card from every suit)?

hints: With 5 cards and 4 suits, one suit must appear twice. Which suit, which 2 cards, and then one card from each other suit.

encounters.title: The Ace Hunt
encounters.story: A shuffled deck is turned over card by card.

phases.ask: P(the first ace is the 14th card)?

hints: Symmetry: is position 14 special compared to position 1?
First ace at 14: the first 13 cards have no ace, then card 14 is an ace.
solution: Any single position is an ace with probability 4/52.

encounters.title: Last Stone Standing
encounters.story: Stones are pulled one by one from a sack of {r} red and {b} blue until it is empty.

phases.ask: P(all the reds are gone before all the blues)?

hints: Reds run out first exactly when… which colour is the very last stone?
solution: The last stone is blue with probability b/(r+b).
encounters.pattern: reframe the event as 'what is last'

encounters.title: The Trickster's Dice
encounters.story: The trickster offers three dice. A = {2,2,4,4,9,9}, B = {1,1,6,6,8,8}, C = {3,3,5,5,7,7}. He lets you pick second. He picks A.

phases.ask: Which die should you pick against A? (choose)

hints: Build the 6×6 win grid (or a 3×3 grid of distinct values) for each pairing.
Check B vs A, C vs A. Pick the one that beats A more than half the time.
solution: P(B beats A) = 4/9; P(C beats A) = 5/9; P(B beats C) = 5/9; P(A beats B) = 5/9 — no die is 'best'.

encounters.title: The Whispered Roll
encounters.story: Two dice are rolled behind a curtain. A spy whispers: 'they show different numbers.'

phases.ask: P(at least one six | different numbers)?

hints: Shrink the 6×6 grid to the cells that match the whisper. How many cells are left, and how many of those contain a 6?

encounters.title: The Ordered Draw
encounters.story: A pouch has {w} white and {b} black pearls. You draw 4 without replacement.

phases.ask: P(first two white, last two black)?

hints: Multiplication rule: P(E1E2E3E4) = P(E1)P(E2|E1)P(E3|E1E2)…
solution: Chain the conditional probabilities draw by draw.

encounters.title: Two Dragon Eggs
encounters.story: A nest has two eggs; each hatches a female or male dragon with probability 1/2, independently.

phases.ask: The OLDER egg is female. P(both female)?
You only learn that AT LEAST ONE is female. P(both female)?

hints: List the sample space {FF, FM, MF, MM} (older first). Which outcomes survive each piece of news?
solution: At least one female: {FF, FM, MF} → 1/3.
encounters.pattern: what exactly was observed changes the conditioning set

encounters.title: The Breeding Pouch
encounters.story: A magic pouch has {w} white and {b} black beads. Each drawn bead is returned along with {c} more of its colour.

phases.ask: P(the first three draws are all white)?

hints: The pouch changes after each draw: update both the white count and the total.
For the second draw, condition on the first and simplify. Notice anything surprising?
solution: Chain rule with the updated counts.
encounters.pattern: Pólya urn: update counts; symmetry across draws

encounters.title: Late for Guard Duty
encounters.story: It rains tomorrow with probability {r}. On a rainy day the guard is late with probability {a}; otherwise with probability {c}.
hints: Draw the tree: weather first, then late or not.
Bayes: the share of 'late' probability that comes through the rain branch.

encounters.title: The Healer's Test
encounters.story: A plague affects {p} of the town. The healer's test detects it {s} of the time, but also flags {fp} of healthy people.

phases.ask: A villager tests positive. P(has the plague)?

hints: Imagine 1000 villagers. How many are sick and test positive? How many are healthy and test positive?

encounters.title: Three Coins in the Box
encounters.story: A box holds a two-headed coin, a fair coin, and a coin that lands heads with probability {q}. One is picked at random and lands heads.
hints: Bayes with three hypotheses: weight each coin by P(heads | coin).

encounters.title: Gold in the Other Drawer
encounters.story: Chest A has gold in both drawers; chest B has gold in one and silver in the other. You open a random drawer of a random chest and see gold.

phases.ask: P(the other drawer of that chest also has gold)?

hints: Count the gold drawers you could have opened. How many of them belong to chest A?
solution: 3 equally likely gold drawers; 2 are in chest A → 2/3.
encounters.pattern: count equally likely observations, not objects

encounters.title: The Transfer Spell
encounters.story: Urn I: 3 white, 2 red. Urn II: 2 white, 3 red. A ball moves from I to II, then you draw from II.

phases.ask: Given that it's white, P(the transferred ball was white)?

hints: Condition on the colour of the transferred ball.
encounters.pattern: condition on the hidden middle step

encounters.title: The Colour Trial
encounters.story: {m} of men and {w} of women in the realm are colour-blind; there are equal numbers of each. A colour-blind person is chosen.
hints: With equal priors, the 1/2s cancel.

encounters.title: Three Prisoners of the Keep
encounters.story: One of three prisoners A, B, C will be exiled, chosen at random. The jailer tells A one of the OTHERS who will stay free, picking at random if both are free. He says 'B'.

phases.ask: P(A is exiled | jailer said B)?
P(C is exiled | jailer said B)?

hints: Compute P(jailer says B | A exiled), P(jailer says B | C exiled), P(jailer says B | B exiled).
solution: Likelihoods ½, 1, 0 with priors ⅓ each → posteriors ⅓, ⅔, 0 (same logic as Monty Hall).
encounters.pattern: the informant's rule matters (Monty Hall logic)

encounters.title: The Balanced Academy
encounters.story: The academy has 3 first-year boys, 6 first-year girls and 5 second-year boys.

phases.ask: How many second-year girls are needed for 'sex' and 'year' to be independent for a randomly chosen student?

hints: Independence means P(boy | first-year) = P(boy | second-year).

encounters.title: The Bridge Circuit
encounters.story: A rune-circuit has gate 1 in series with a parallel pair of gates 2 and 3. Gates work independently with probabilities {p1}, {p2}, {p3}.
hints: Series → all must work (multiply). Parallel → at least one works (1 − all fail).

encounters.title: The Five Wards
encounters.story: A shield holds while at least {k} of its {n} wards work. Each ward works independently with probability {p}.
hints: The number of working wards is binomial. Which values count as a success?

encounters.title: Best of Seven
encounters.story: Your champion wins each bout with probability {p}, independently. The first to 4 wins takes the title.

phases.ask: P(the match goes the full 7 bouts)?

hints: Your champion wins in exactly k bouts if bout k is a win and exactly 3 of the first k−1 are wins.
Seven bouts happen exactly when the first six are split 3–3.

encounters.title: The Simultaneous Duel
encounters.story: You and the bandit fire at the same time each round. You hit with probability {a}, he hits with probability {b}. If both miss, you fire again.

phases.ask: P(you are the only one hit when the duel ends)?

hints: Rounds where both miss just restart the game. Condition on the round that ends it.
solution: P(you only hit, in the final round) = (1−a)b/(1 − (1−a)(1−b)).
encounters.pattern: restart → condition on the ending round

encounters.title: The Ferry Toll Game
encounters.story: You and the ferryman take turns rolling two dice, you first. You win as soon as you roll a sum of 8; he wins as soon as he rolls a 7.
hints: Look at one full cycle (your roll, then his). Either someone wins in the cycle or it repeats.
solution: P(win) = P(win on your roll) / P(the cycle ends) = (5/36) / (1 − (31/36)(30/36)).
encounters.pattern: alternating trials → geometric series / cycle trick

encounters.title: The Gambler's Ledge
encounters.story: You hold {i} gold. Each bet wins 1 gold with probability {p} or loses 1. You stop when broke or at {N} gold.
hints: Let P_i = P(success from i gold). Condition on the first bet: P_i = pP_{i+1} + qP_{i−1}.
Solve the recursion, or use the gambler's ruin formula.

encounters.title: The Queen's Secret
encounters.story: The queen carries a hidden curse with probability 1/2. If she does, each prince inherits it with probability 1/2. Her {k} princes are all free of it.
hints: Likelihood of 'k clean princes' under each hypothesis?

encounters.title: The Withered Herb
encounters.story: Your neighbour waters your herb with probability {w}. Unwatered, it dies with probability {d1}; watered, with probability {d2}. You return to find it dead.

phases.ask: P(the herb survives), before you look?
P(the neighbour forgot | the herb died)?

hints: Tree: watered or not, then dies or not.

encounters.title: An Ace for Every Hand
encounters.story: A deck is dealt into 4 hands of 13.

phases.ask: P(each hand gets exactly one ace)?

hints: Track the aces one at a time: where does ace 2 go relative to ace 1? Then ace 3…
solution: Ace 2 avoids ace 1's hand: 39/51; ace 3: 26/50; ace 4: 13/49 → ≈ 0.105.

encounters.title: Which Coin?
encounters.story: You pick one of two coins at random; one lands heads with probability {p1}, the other with {p2}. Two flips: both heads.
hints: Flips are independent GIVEN the coin, but not unconditionally.
Next-flip probability = posterior-weighted average.

encounters.title: The Bookmaker
encounters.story: A rider wins with probability 3/8.

phases.ask: What are the odds in favour of the rider, as a single number?

hints: Odds = P(E)/P(E^c).

encounters.title: The Friend's Two Cards
encounters.story: A friend draws two cards.

phases.ask: She says 'at least one is an ace'. P(both aces)?
She says 'one is the ace of spades'. P(both aces)?

hints: Count the hands that match each statement. The statements are not equally informative!
encounters.pattern: specific information conditions differently from vague information

encounters.title: The Pearl Bet
encounters.story: A jar has {w} white, {b} black and {o} gold pearls. You draw 2. You win 3 coins per black pearl and lose 1 per white one; gold pays nothing.
hints: List the possible pairs (WW, WB, BB, WO, BO, OO), the winnings for each, and their probabilities.
Shortcut: by linearity, E = 2 × (expected value of a single draw).
solution: +2 only from one white + one black.
encounters.pattern: build the PMF from the cases; or use linearity

encounters.title: The Higher Bone
encounters.story: Roll a die twice; X is the larger value.
hints: P(X ≤ m) = (m/6)². So what is P(X = m)?

encounters.title: The Caravan Insurance
encounters.story: You insure a caravan: you pay {A} if it is raided this year, which happens with probability {p}.

phases.ask: What premium gives an expected profit of 10% of A?

hints: E[profit] = premium − A·p.

encounters.title: Faulty Arrows
encounters.story: A quiver has {N} arrows; {D} are warped. You grab {n}.

phases.ask: Expected number of warped arrows grabbed?

hints: Indicator for each grabbed arrow: P(warped) = ?

encounters.title: The Moment Scale
encounters.story: A random weight X has E[X] = {m} and Var(X) = {s2}.
hints: E[X²] = Var(X) + (E[X])².
Var(a + bX) = b²Var(X).

encounters.title: Pooled Potions Test
encounters.story: {N} soldiers are tested for a fever in groups of {g}: one pooled test per group, and if it's positive, everyone in that group is retested individually. Each soldier has the fever independently with probability {p}.
hints: One group: always 1 test, plus g more if anyone is sick. P(someone sick) = ?
solution: Per group: 1 + g(1 − (1−p)^g). Multiply by N/g groups.
encounters.pattern: expected cost via a per-unit indicator

encounters.title: The Blindfold Exam
encounters.story: An exam has {n} riddles with {c} options each. You guess blindly.
hints: Number correct ~ Binomial(n, 1/c).
solution: Binomial tail from k to n.

encounters.title: The Seer's Claim
encounters.story: A seer claims second sight. A fair coin is flipped {n} times and she gets {k} or more right.

phases.ask: P(at least {k} right by pure luck)?

hints: If she has no gift, her number correct is Binomial(n, 1/2).

encounters.title: Reverse Engineering
encounters.story: A binomial count has mean 8 and variance 4.8.
hints: np = 8 and np(1−p) = 4.8. Divide the second by the first.
encounters.pattern: solve for (n, p) from the moments

encounters.title: The Council of Judges
encounters.story: {n} judges each reach the right verdict independently with probability {p}. The majority decides.
hints: The majority is right when at least (n+1)/2 judges are right.

encounters.title: The Scribe's Errors
encounters.story: The royal scribe averages {l} errors per page.

phases.ask: P(a page has 2 or more errors)?

hints: Rare events across many opportunities → which distribution?

encounters.title: The Lottery of 400
encounters.story: {n} independent lottery tickets each win with probability {p}.
hints: λ = np.
solution: Poisson(np) is a good approximation when n is large and p is small.

encounters.title: Gate Arrivals
encounters.story: Travellers reach the gate at an average rate of 1 every {r} minutes.
hints: Scale the rate to the window: λ = window/r.
encounters.pattern: Poisson with the rate scaled to the time window

encounters.title: Waiting for the Six
encounters.story: You roll a die until the first six.

phases.ask: P(the first six is on roll {k})?

hints: k−1 failures and then a success.

encounters.title: The Third Victory
encounters.story: You win each joust with probability {p}. You keep jousting until your {r}rd win.
hints: The last joust must be a win; place the other r−1 wins among the first n−1 jousts.

encounters.title: The Inspector's Crates
encounters.story: A crate of {N} lanterns has {D} broken ones. The inspector tests {n} at random and accepts the crate only if all {n} work.
hints: Sampling without replacement → hypergeometric with 0 broken.

encounters.title: The Red-Bet System
encounters.story: A 'sure-win' system: bet 1 on red (P = 18/38). If you win, stop. If you lose, bet 1 on red twice more, then stop.
hints: List the outcomes: W; LWW; LWL/LLW; LLL. What is the net result of each?
Is P(ahead) > ½ while E < 0 a contradiction?
solution: E ≈ −0.108: you win small often and lose big rarely.

encounters.title: The Staircase Scroll
hints: Jump sizes are the PMF.
P(a < X ≤ b) = F(b) − F(a).
encounters.pattern: read the PMF off the CDF jumps

encounters.title: First to Two
encounters.story: Two knights duel until one has 2 wins. You win each bout with probability {p}.
hints: The match lasts 2 bouts if the first two have the same winner; otherwise 3.

encounters.title: Who Pays for Mead?
encounters.story: Three friends flip coins; the 'odd one out' pays. If all three match, they flip again.
hints: P(all match) = 2/8. Rounds until the first 'odd one out' is geometric.

encounters.title: The Spice Speculator
encounters.story: You hold 1000 coins. Spice costs 2 coins an ounce today; next week it will cost 1 or 4, each with probability 1/2.

phases.ask: Buy everything now: expected value of your spice next week, in coins?
To maximise the expected OUNCES you hold, wait a week then buy: expected ounces?
Which goal do you pursue if you plan to sell next week? (choose)

hints: Expected value is linear in what you are measuring. Measure coins in one case and ounces in the other.
solution: If you'll sell for coins, maximise coins: buy now.
encounters.pattern: which quantity are you taking the expectation of?

encounters.title: The Shaped Fog
encounters.story: A fog's position X has density f(x) = c(1 − x²) on (−1, 1).
hints: A density must integrate to 1.
Integrate the density from 0.5 to 1.

encounters.title: The Leaning Tower
encounters.story: X has density f(x) = 2x on (0, 1).
hints: E[X] = ∫x f(x)dx; E[X²] = ∫x² f(x)dx.

encounters.title: The Coach Stop
encounters.story: The coach arrives at a time uniform over the next {T} minutes.

phases.ask: It hasn't come after {t0} minutes. P(you wait at least {more} more)?

hints: Uniform: probability = length/total length.
Given it hasn't come by t0, the arrival is uniform on what's left.
solution: Uniform on (t0, T): (T − t0 − more)/(T − t0). Unlike the exponential, this has memory!
encounters.pattern: uniform: length ratios; conditioning keeps it uniform

encounters.title: The Hidden Range
encounters.story: X is uniform on (a, b) with E[X] = {m} and Var(X) = {v}.
hints: Var = (b − a)²/12 and E = (a + b)/2.

encounters.title: The Archery Range
encounters.story: Your arrows land at a distance ~ N({mu}, {s}²) from the line.

phases.ask: P(within one σ of the mean)?

hints: Standardise: Z = (X − μ)/σ, then use the Φ-scroll.

encounters.title: The Top 5%
encounters.story: Mage-trial scores are N({mu}, {s}²). Only the top 5% earn a staff.

phases.ask: What is the cutoff score? (Use z = 1.645.)

hints: Find z with Φ(z) = 0.95, then un-standardise.

encounters.title: Six Hundred Rolls
encounters.story: A die is rolled {n} times. Let X = the number of sixes.

phases.ask: Normal approximation (with continuity correction) of P({lo} ≤ X ≤ {hi})?

hints: Integer values from lo to hi → stretch the interval to lo − 0.5 and hi + 0.5.

encounters.title: The Ferryman's Service
encounters.story: The ferryman's service time is exponential with mean {m} minutes.

phases.ask: You have already waited {a} minutes. P(more than {t} additional minutes)?

hints: Exponential: P(X > t) = e^(−λt) with λ = 1/mean.
Memoryless.
solution: Same: the exponential forgets the past.

encounters.title: The Ageing Golem
encounters.story: A golem's hazard rate is λ(t) = t² (it wears out faster as it ages).
hints: P(X > t) = exp(−∫₀ᵗ λ(s)ds).

encounters.title: The Log Transmutation
encounters.story: U is uniform on (0, 1). The alchemist forms Y = −ln U.
solution: P(U < e^(−y)) = e^(−y): Y is Exp(1).

encounters.title: The Root Riddle
encounters.story: Y is uniform on (0, {L}). Consider 4x² + 4Yx + (Y + 6) = 0.
hints: Real roots ⇔ discriminant ≥ 0. Turn that into a condition on Y.
encounters.pattern: turn the event into an interval

encounters.title: Wagon Wheels
encounters.story: Wagon-wheel lifetimes are N({mu}, {s}²) leagues.

phases.ask: P(lasts beyond 48000 | it has already lasted 45000)?

hints: Conditional = P(both) / P(given). Here 'beyond 48000' implies 'beyond 45000'.
solution: Ratio of the two normal tails.

encounters.title: Twin Forge Dice
encounters.story: Two dice: X = the larger value, Y = the sum.
hints: List the cells of the 6×6 grid with max 4 and sum 6.
encounters.pattern: joint PMF from the grid; marginals by summing

encounters.title: The Joint Ledger
hints: Marginal = row sum.
Independent ⇔ every cell = product of its marginals.

encounters.title: The Tilted Square
encounters.story: (X, Y) has density f(x, y) = c(x + y) on the unit square.
hints: ∫∫(x + y) over the square = ?
Integrate over the triangle below x + y = 1.

encounters.title: The Midnight Rendezvous
encounters.story: Two spies each arrive at a time uniform over a {T}-minute window, independently. Each waits {w} minutes, then leaves.
hints: Draw the T×T square of arrival times. Where is |X − Y| ≤ w?
solution: The two corner triangles have total area (T − w)² → 1 − ((T − w)/T)².

encounters.title: Two Sand-Timers
encounters.story: Two independent uniform(0,1) sand-timers X and Y.
hints: The density of the sum is a triangle; or use area in the unit square.

encounters.title: The Bowling Rivals
encounters.story: Asha scores N({m1}, {s1}²) and Bodhi scores N({m2}, {s2}²), independently.
hints: D = Bodhi − Asha is normal. What are its mean and variance?
encounters.pattern: sums/differences of independent normals are normal

encounters.title: Two Roads
encounters.story: Carts on the north road ~ Poisson({a}), on the south road ~ Poisson({b}), independent.

phases.ask: Given {k} carts in total, P(exactly 1 came by the north road)?

hints: The sum of independent Poissons is Poisson.
Conditional on the total → binomial split.
encounters.pattern: Poisson sum; conditional split is binomial

encounters.title: Split Harvest
encounters.story: X₁ ~ Bin({n1}, ½) and X₂ ~ Bin({n2}, ½) are independent. You learn X₁ + X₂ = {t}.
hints: With equal p, the p's cancel, leaving pure counting.
encounters.pattern: conditioning a sum of binomials → hypergeometric

encounters.title: Two Machines
encounters.story: Two mills fail at independent exponential times with rates {l1} and {l2} per hour.

phases.ask: P(no failure in the first {t} hours)?

hints: min of independent exponentials is exponential with summed rate.
Race of exponentials.

encounters.title: Five Sparks
encounters.story: {n} sparks land at independent uniform(0,1) positions.
hints: max < x ⇔ all < x.
E[k-th smallest of n uniforms] = k/(n+1).

encounters.title: Three Stones on a Line
encounters.story: Three stones X₁, X₂, X₃ fall at independent random points on a line segment.

phases.ask: P(X₃ lies between X₁ and X₂)?

hints: By symmetry, each stone is equally likely to be the middle one.

encounters.title: The Shifting Rate
encounters.story: f(x, y) = x·e^(−x(y+1)) for x, y > 0.
hints: f(y | x) = f(x, y)/f_X(x). Recognise the shape in y.
solution: Given X = x, Y ~ Exp(x) → e^(−xy).
encounters.pattern: conditional density: fix x, normalise in y

encounters.title: Helmets Returned
encounters.story: {n} knights get their helmets back at random.

phases.ask: Expected number of knights who get their own helmet?

hints: Indicator I_i: P(I_i = 1) = 1/n. Then Cov(I_i, I_j)?

encounters.title: The Six Runes
encounters.story: Each chest holds one of {k} runes, equally likely. You open chests until you own all {k}.
hints: After i different runes, the wait for a new one is geometric with p = (k − i)/k.
solution: Σ k/(k − i) = k·H_k ≈ 14.7 for k = 6.

encounters.title: Feast Days
encounters.story: {n} villagers have independent uniform birthdays (365 days).
hints: Indicator for each day: is it somebody's birthday?
encounters.pattern: count distinct values via indicators on the values

encounters.title: Empty Barrels
encounters.story: {n} apples are tossed into {n} barrels, each barrel equally likely.
hints: Indicator per barrel: P(empty) = ?

encounters.title: Runs of Fortune
encounters.story: A fair coin is flipped {n} times. A run is a maximal block of equal outcomes.
hints: A new run starts at flip i > 1 exactly when flip i ≠ flip i−1.

encounters.title: Partner Draw
encounters.story: {m} men and {m} women are randomly split into {m} pairs.
hints: Indicator per man: P(his partner is a woman) = ?

encounters.title: Ones and Twos
encounters.story: A die is rolled {n} times; X = number of 1s, Y = number of 2s.
hints: Write X = ΣI_i and Y = ΣJ_i; only same-roll pairs matter.

encounters.title: The Carp Pond
encounters.story: A pond has {N} fish, {K} of them carp. You catch {n}.
hints: Hypergeometric variance = binomial variance × the finite-population correction.

encounters.title: The Miner's Three Doors
encounters.story: A trapped miner picks one of three doors at random each time (he forgets). Door 1 loops back after {a} days, door 2 after {b} days, door 3 leads out in {c} days.
hints: Condition on the first door: E = ⅓(a + E) + ⅓(b + E) + ⅓c.

encounters.title: The Tower Lift
encounters.story: The number of people entering the tower lift is Poisson({lam}). Each picks one of {N} floors at random.

phases.ask: Expected number of floors where the lift stops?

hints: Thinning: arrivals for each floor are Poisson(λ/N).

encounters.title: Accident Ledger
encounters.story: A mine averages {m} accidents a week; each injures {w} miners on average (independently of the count).

encounters.title: The Generating Rune
encounters.story: X has MGF M(t) = exp({l}(eᵗ − 1)).
hints: Recognise the MGF. Which distribution has this form?

encounters.title: Linked Fates
encounters.story: Var(X) = {vx}, Var(Y) = {vy}, Cov(X, Y) = {c}.
hints: Var(aX + bY) = a²VarX + b²VarY + 2abCov.

encounters.title: Both Faces
encounters.story: A coin (heads probability {p}) is flipped until both heads and tails have appeared.
hints: Condition on the first flip, then wait for the other face (geometric).

encounters.title: The Tower of Bounds I
encounters.story: Daily tribute X ≥ 0 has mean {m}. Nothing else is known.

phases.ask: Best Markov upper bound on P(X ≥ {a})?

hints: Markov: P(X ≥ a) ≤ E[X]/a.

encounters.title: The Tower of Bounds II
encounters.story: Now you also know Var(X) = {v}.

phases.ask: Chebyshev lower bound on P({m}−{k} < X < {m}+{k})?

hints: P(|X − μ| ≥ k) ≤ σ²/k².

encounters.title: The Hundred-Dice Army
encounters.story: {n} soldiers each roll a die; the general sums the results.
hints: One die: μ = 3.5, σ² = 35/12. A sum of n dice: nμ, nσ².

encounters.title: The Tax Collector's Rounding
encounters.story: {n} amounts are rounded to the nearest coin; each error is uniform on (−½, ½).

phases.ask: P(the total error exceeds {d} in absolute value)?

hints: Var of one uniform(−½, ½) error = 1/12.

encounters.title: Lanterns Through the Night
encounters.story: {n} lanterns burn one after another; each lasts an exponential time with mean {m} hours.

phases.ask: P(total light lasts more than {T} hours)?

hints: Exponential: σ = mean.

encounters.title: The Guild Insurer
encounters.story: {n} policies each have a yearly claim with mean {m} and standard deviation {s}.
hints: Standard deviation of the total = σ√n.

encounters.title: How Many Recruits?
encounters.story: Recruit scores have standard deviation {s}. How many recruits are needed so that their average is within {d} of the true mean with 95% probability?
hints: Solve 1.96·σ/√n ≤ d for n.

encounters.title: The Hundred Wagers
encounters.story: Each wager: lose 1 (0.7), lose 2 (0.2), or win 10 (0.1). You make 100 wagers.
hints: Var = E[X²] − (E[X])².
Ahead means total ≥ 1; use the continuity correction at 0.5.

encounters.title: The Law Itself
encounters.story: A fair coin is flipped n times. Using Chebyshev, how large must n be so that P(|average − ½| ≥ {eps}) ≤ {a}?
hints: Var(average) = (1/4)/n.

encounters.title: Swarm Count
encounters.story: A swarm count is Poisson({l}).

phases.ask: Normal approximation of P(X ≥ {k}) (with continuity correction)?

hints: Poisson(λ): mean λ, variance λ.
